newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Puts sold in Railtrack on rally.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Puts sold in Railtrack on rally.

text.p: Nearly 800 Railtrack puts were sold at various strikes on Thursday as the underlying shares climbed further into unchartered territory, dealers said.
"Just about everyone is bullish on that stock," said one. "Professionals are selling the puts and collecting the premium."
The most actively traded options on Railtrack were the March 330, the June 300 and the June 390 puts.

By 1542 GMT, Railtrack shares were up 26p to 396-1/2p amid a bear squeeze and talk of U.S. buying. The shares have been buoyed in recent weeks by talk of revaluation of the company's substantial property portfolio.

British Telecommunications options were among the most actively traded. Dealers noted an aggressively bullish trade whereby more than 1,000 May 390 calls were purchased and more than 1,000 May 390 puts were sold. A total of about 2,600 calls and about 1,400 puts changing hands.
Shares in British Telecommunications firmed 6p to 399-1/2p, just 8p shy of their high for the year.
Dealers also noted put sales in some of the major UK banks, whose shares have been rising recently amid expectations higher mortgage rates will translate into wider profit margins.
They said puts were sold on Abbey National Bank and Lloyds tsb and Barclays Bank. Abbey National and Lloyds have particularly high exposure to the mortgage market.

Abbey shares were up 3-1/2p to 740-1/2p after having climbed to a fresh record peak at 750p earlier. Lloyds shares were up 1p to 426-1/2p, while Barclays sank 7-1/2p to 1008p after having risen to a record earlier at 1050p.
Index options and futures trading was mostly linked to roll over ahead of December expiry tomorrow.
